|\n\n...\n\nA1 Basis of preparation of Interim Financial Report \n\n The interim financial report is unaudited and has been prepared in compliance with Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (\"MFRS\") 134, Interim Financial Reporting issued by the Malaysian Accounting Standards Board, Paragraph 9.22 and Appendix 9B of the Listing Requirements of Bursa Malaysia Securities Berhad. \n\n The interim financial report should be read in conjunction with the audited financial statements of the Group for the financial year ended 31 December 2025 and the accompanying explanatory notes attached to this interim financial report. \n\n The significant accounting policies and method of computation adopted in the interim financial report are consistent with those adopted in the annual financial statements for the financial year ended 31 December 2025 except for the adoption of the following MFRSs:- \n\n Effective for annual periods beginning on or after \n\n Amendments to MFRS 9 and MFRS 7 Amendments to the Classification and Measurement of Financial Instruments\n\n Amendments to MFRS 9 and MFRS 7 Contracts Referencing Nature-dependent\n\n...\n\n1 January 2026 \n\n 1 January 2026 \n\n yet effective:- \n\n MFRS (issued as at the end of the reporting period) \n\n Effective for annual periods beginning on or after \n\n MFRS 18 Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements 1 January 2027 MFRS 19 Subsidiaries without Public Accountability: Disclosures 1 January 2027 \n\n Amendments to MFRS 10 and MFRS 128 Sale or Contribution of Assets between an Investor and its Associate or Joint Venture\n\n Amendments to MFRS 121 Translation to a Hyperinflationary Presentation Currency\n\n...\n\nB1 Review of performance \n\n Current quarter \n\n Corresponding preceding quarter \n\n ended \n\n 30-Jun-26 \n\n 30-Jun-25 \n\n Changes \n\n Revenue \n\n 374,915 \n\n 183,043 \n\n 191,872 \n\n 104.8% \n\n Profit before tax \n\n 99,946 \n\n 37,907 \n\n 62,039 \n\n 163.7% \n\n Profit for the financial period \n\n 84,495 \n\n 27,807 \n\n 56,688 \n\n 203.9% \n\n Profit attributable to owners of \n\n the Company \n\n 85,043 \n\n 28,133 \n\n 56,910 \n\n 202.3% \n\n The Group's revenue for the quarter under review achieved a stellar expansion of 104.8% or RM191.9 million, surging from RM183.0 million in the corresponding preceding quarter to RM374.9 million. This remarkable top-line performance was primarily driven by explosive Artificial Intelligence (\"AI\") infrastructure demand, our strategic focus into high-value, resilient markets like automotive, and consumer electronics and accelerated global supply chain restructuring which has deepened customer engagements. Our focus on advanced packaging and high-precision inspection solutions directly addresses the increasing complexities of AI accelerators and High Bandwidth Memory (\"HBM\") mirroring the strong momentum seen in the broader semiconductors and electronics manufacturing sector and enabling us to expand our output far beyond the previous year's low baseline. \n\n Profit before tax (\"PBT\") for the individual quarter surged by 163.7% or RM62.0 million, soaring to RM99.9 million from RM37.9 million due to structural manufacturing scale and a highly favourable product mix. Profit after tax (\"PAT\") rose by 203.9% or RM56.7 million, increasing from RM27.8 million to RM84.5 million. This bottom-line outperformance reflects exceptional operational optimization across the facilities alongside the sustained positive impact of income tax exemption enjoyed by the key subsidiary ViTrox Technologies Sdn. Bhd. (\"VTSB\").\n\n...\n\nThe Group cumulative revenue achieved a robust expansion of 98.0% to RM642.0 million, a result of our steadfast commitment to disciplined execution and long-term value creation. We have successfully seized the momentum from strong AI infrastructure demands, alongside growing needs in the automotive and consumer electronics sectors. By leveraging our deep and broad customer base spanning over 30 countries, we continue to deliver advanced Automated Board Inspection (\"ABI\") and Machine Vision System (\"MVS\") solutions that meet the evolving requirements of our global partners with humility and focus. \n\n In tandem with this growth, cumulative PBT rose by 147.4% to RM161.6 million, while PAT climbed 161.6% to RM135.3 million. These results underscore our commitment to operational excellence and disciplined cost management, securing our strong financial position as we scale."],"summary":"Summary:\n\n- ViTrox Corporation Berhad (Malaysia) released its interim financial report for the second quarter ended 30 June 2026 (unaudited, compliant with MFRS 134).\n- Key highlights:\n  - Revenue: RM 641.97 million year-to-date (6M) up from RM 324.16 million prior-year period; The company's latest outlook paints an optimistic picture for 2026, driven by explosive demand for artificial intelligence (AI), massive investments in data centres, and a sharp recovery in the chip memory market. A Golden Era for the Semiconductor Industry According to Gartner, the global semiconductor market is expected to expand by an astonishing 64% in 2026, surpassing US$1.3 trillion in annual revenue. Several powerful growth drivers are supporting this expansion: AI is becoming the industry's biggest growth engine. AI-related semiconductors are expected to contribute around 30% of total semiconductor revenue. Memory chip prices are experiencing a strong recovery, boosting industry revenue. Demand continues to accelerate as cloud computing and AI applications become increasingly widespread. These structural trends are expected to create long-term opportunities across the semiconductor value chain. Hyperscalers Continue to Spend Aggressively Global technology giants are showing no signs of slowing their AI investments. ViTrox highlighted that hyperscaler spending on AI infrastructure is projected to increase by more than 50%, driving demand for: High-performance GPUs AI accelerators Specialised non-GPU processors Advanced semiconductor manufacturing technologies As semiconductor complexity increases, manufacturers require increasingly sophisticated inspection equipment to maintain quality and yield. Advanced Packaging: ViTrox's Next Growth Engine One of the most exciting opportunities lies in advanced semiconductor packaging. As chips become smaller, more powerful and more complex, manufacturers require: Ultra-high inspection accuracy Higher-resolution imaging More precise defect detection Faster production inspection This is precisely where ViTrox sees significant growth potential. QX1 Series: Designed for the Next Generation of Chip Manufacturing To capture this expanding market, ViTrox has introduced its new QX1 Series. The new platform is designed to provide: Ultra-high-resolution 3D X-ray inspection Inspection of miniature and highly complex components Advanced packaging applications Electronics assembly inspection The QX1 Series strengthens ViTrox's product portfolio and positions the company to benefit from the industry's migration toward increasingly advanced semiconductor manufacturing technologies. Growth with Financial Discipline Despite the favourable industry outlook, ViTrox remains disciplined in its execution. Management continues to focus on: Proactive cost management Operational efficiency Protecting profit margins Managing currency volatility Navigating geopolitical uncertainties This balanced strategy allows the company to pursue growth opportunities while maintaining financial resilience. Key Takeaways for Investors ViTrox's 2026 outlook highlights several important themes: The semiconductor industry is entering a powerful expansion cycle. AI is becoming the primary driver of industry growth. The global semiconductor market is projected to exceed US$1.3 trillion. Hyperscaler AI spending is expected to rise by more than 50%. Advanced packaging is emerging as one of the industry's fastest-growing segments. ViTrox's new QX1 Series is strategically positioned to capitalise on this trend. Cost discipline and prudent operational management remain priorities despite the optimistic outlook. Conclusion While short-term market sentiment may continue to fluctuate due to geopolitical developments, currency movements and macroeconomic uncertainty, ViTrox's long-term growth story remains firmly supported by structural industry trends. Revenue was up more than 110% year-on-year to RM485.1 million.\n\nLooking ahead, ViTrox expects a favourable business environment for the remainder of the financial year and into 2027, supported by robust growth in the semiconductor sector, continued investment in data centre infrastructure and rising demand for edge artificial intelligence (AI) devices.\n\nThe company — which makes machines used to automatically inspect and detect defects in semiconductor components and printed circuit board assemblies — said it is seeking to capture a slice of the increasing complexity of AI accelerators and high bandwidth memory.\n\nNet profit in the first nine months of the year also jumped to RM254.8 million from RM87 million a year earlier, supported by sustained capital expenditure deployment from strong AI infrastructure demand and electronics manufacturing customers.\n\nRevenue for the period also more than doubled to RM1.13 billion from RM552.7 million.\n\n“The group will continue to exercise prudent cost management and operational discipline to mitigate potential risks from foreign exchange volatility and geopolitical uncertainties,” ViTrox said.\n\nNo interim dividend was declared for the quarter under review, though the company had paid out 1.18 sen per share in July.\n\nShares of ViTrox ended Thursday at RM10.60, down 30 sen or 2.8%, giving the Penang-based company a market capitalisation of RM20 billion ahead of the results announcement. \n\nThe content is a snapshot from Publisher.
